observations.finding: Exact DOI 10.1007/s40121-026-01362-z, PMID 42236640 and 15-author byline agree across received report, supplement and metadata. EPMC identifies PMCID PMC13280275, volume15 issue7 pages1955–1976; online June3 2026 and print July2026 differ as publication dates, not identity conflicts.

Crossref relation is empty and neither received exact-identifier response supplies a linked correction, retraction or concern notice. General update-policy URL and EPMC metadata-revision date are not correction notices. Indexed abstract repeats the source attribution conflict. This is a dated bounded metadata inspection, not exhaustive integrity surveillance.

Retrospective Singapore population-registry cohort of people with type2 diabetes and first COVID infection July1 2021–February28 2023. Prior antidiabetic prescriptions within12months define prevalent exposures. No randomization or causal treatment assignment; comparator is users of other antidiabetic drugs, not untreated people.

152727 initially eligible registry records; exclusions printed: missing demographics402, age under18 303, no prior-year antidiabetic use62028, chronic renal disease13615, death within30days462, reinfection within300days2517, non-mRNA vaccination1702. Final71698; metformin66792 versus4906, SGLT222501 versus49197, DPP417039 versus54659, sulfonylurea32016 versus39682. These are overlapping drug partitions of one cohort, not separate studies. Outcome-specific populations exclude history within5years and vary by endpoint.

Index is first infection; analysis considers days31–300, not initiation of drug after long-COVID diagnosis. Excluding early deaths and later reinfection conditions on postbaseline events; survivor/selection bias remains possible. Death/loss accounted for in models is not a complete numerical attrition report.

Prescription-record exposure does not establish dose, route, formulation, adherence or sustained duration. Concurrent medications allowed. Metformin with SGLT2 versus metformin without SGLT2 should not be called metformin-alone versus combination when other drugs may remain.

Administrative ICD diagnosis/symptom outcomes are heterogeneous proxies and do not establish independently adjudicated patient-reported long-COVID syndrome. Extensive code lists are supplied, but no obvious standalone GI/dermatological aggregate mapping or abdominal/pelvic/generalized-pain mapping is shown. Printed code-description and duplicate-code anomalies are retained as reporting limitations; no external codebook validation or invented corrections.

Overlap propensity weighting uses measured demographic, vaccination, comorbidity, medication, HbA1c/eGFR and acute-COVID variables; standardized differences rounded to0 after weighting are not proof of no residual confounding. Adjustment for hospitalization/current COVID treatment may condition on mediators/colliders. HbA1c/eGFR information-not-available categories appear; missing demographic records excluded. No assumption of multiple imputation. Exact propensity equations, positivity diagnostics and named competing-risk estimand are not fully reported.

Main narrative reports90–300-day neurological/memory findings forSGLT2(p0.0014/0.0017) and metformin composite/symptoms(p0.0391/0.0436). No assigned supplemental table gives full effect/CI/event counts for this window. Report as incomplete sensitivity reporting, not reconstructed numerical verification.

Authors use95%CIexcluding1 for significance andp<0.01 as more robust to multiplicity. This is not a demonstrated formal multiplicity-control procedure. Numerous outcomes/subgroups, sparse cells and suppressed counts warrant caution. Subgroup significance differences do not prove interaction; no invented power calculation or MCID.

No accessible registered protocol, SAP, full analysis code, dataset, model coefficients/diagnostics, detailed loss/death counts, validated minimal clinically important difference or comprehensive drug adverse-event/discontinuation ascertainment. Reporting omissions after full inspection are genuine not_reported, not proof procedures never occurred.

Authors state IRB approval not required for national-surveillance analysis under Infectious Diseases Act, Helsinki adherence and all15authors no competing interests. NationalMOH/NMRC grants listed. Publication-fee text attributes payment both to NCID/TanTockSengHospital and later authors; preserve reporting ambiguity. Individual data unavailable, deidentified sharing subjectMOHapproval; no supplied code. Funding does not itself establish bias or misconduct.

Qualitative design-appropriate appraisal only: residual confounding, prevalent-user/indication bias, selection, administrative measurement and multiplicity constrain causal interpretation. Highly vaccinated Singapore T2DM population/prior medication use does not establish initiating metformin/SGLT2 for established longCOVID, nondiabetic patients or clinical safety. Mechanistic discussion relies on background literature, not direct mechanisms measured here.

Complete reference list read as context; cited studies were not separately inspected/acquired. One cohort with overlapping drug groups/outcomes/subsets does not create multiple independent studies; historical resultIDs remain preserved. No claim of exhaustive replication search or formalGRADE/ROBINS-I rating.
